title: Toon of Mythos delegation policy
description: Shape of policy/delegation.json, the validated transition artifact generated from policy/dhall/delegation.dhall. Owner: TIN-2698. This describes the Jesssullivan/prompt-toon delegation policy only; tinyland-inc/lab ships a same-named policy/delegation.json with an unrelated interview-HITL schema.

$comment.description: Provenance banner naming the Dhall source of truth and its regeneration command.

providers.description: Provider allow-list (TIN-7760). Each entry names the exact model ids a seat on that provider may run, its access path and its endpoints. Model ids are keyed by endpoint. A seat whose provider, endpoint or model id is not admitted fails closed.

model_ids.description: The model ids on this provider's admitted endpoints. A forbidden endpoint's ids never appear here.

endpoints.description: Access paths to the provider, each with the model ids it uses. A refused endpoint is listed with admitted false so a consumer can recognise and refuse it.

seats.description: First-class seat records. Seat names are load-bearing routing identities, not free-form model_classes strings.

model_id.description: Exact model the seat runs (J81). Omitted for a provider-managed seat such as fable.

model_id_source.description: Where the seat's model id comes from. pinned: this policy names it. account-config: a config value read from the account after login and never written here (TIN-7125). Only fable is account-config.

provider.description: The providers[] entry whose allow-list admits this seat's model_id.

endpoint.description: The admitted provider endpoint whose model_ids hold this seat's model_id. Omitted for Anthropic seats, whose ids do not vary by endpoint.

harness_seats.description: Agent-harness dispatch identities Fable or Cade may delegate bounded work to. A harness seat is not a model class and never appears in a persona's model_classes: it names the harness, the model lane it rides, the exact task envelope it may receive, the surface dispatch must go through, the fixed launcher behind a transport surface, and its posture.

launcher.description: The fixed launcher behind a transport surface such as an swb recipient. Omitted when the surface is itself the launcher.

posture.description: evidentiary-only: the output is evidence for the synthesis seat or the Opus merge gate. gated-worker: the Cade job seat's output is work product whose external acts wait for a GO. No harness seat carries the operator WORD leg or gates a merge.

persona.description: A persona id, or a harness seat id for a mythos.delegate.* lane.

budget_fallbacks.description: Seat downgrades allowed when a seat's quota is exhausted (J81(e)). Each names the personas and the exact lanes it reaches plus the obligations the downgraded lane carries. A fallback never reaches fable or haiku, the adversarial persona, the merge gate or a host act. It always carries the merge, host-act and receipt obligations.

lanes.description: Every route the fallback reaches. A lane of a covered persona that is not listed keeps its default seat.

cade.description: Cade orchestration (TIN-7760, TIN-7125): the orchestrator, the advisory cross-provider review, the auto-level child rule, custody classes, the cade.* lanes, the broker and dispatch.

seat_resolution.description: A child's effective seats are its lane's default and alternate seats, in that order, that also sit in its parent home's custody class.

on_no_seat.description: When no effective seat remains the child waits. It never borrows a seat from outside its parent home's custody.

harness_seats.description: Harness seats that may see this class's data. Child seat resolution reads seats only. SPR-182 puts every Kimi seat, pi-k3 included, in the ops class.

broker.description: The Cade broker (TIN-7125, new policy). Kimi may route a request to a cade.* lane and author cade.dispatch/v1 envelopes. It gates nothing, never names a model and never sets custody.

gates.description: What the broker may gate: nothing.

writes.description: Envelope fields the broker writes. Cade's own code stamps the rest, custody from the source item's label included.

dispatch.description: Cade dispatch (TIN-7125): the shared envelope and receipt contract, transport, root resolution, carve-out reroute and inheritance, custody narrowing, units, the Fable id, the job seat, effects, credentials and accounting. Nothing here caps count, depth or cost.

recipient.description: The 4-part swb id. swb accepts only <harness>:<host>:<pid>:<session_id> ids, and pid 1 is fixed so the address never changes.

receiver.description: Receiver authority (wire contract section 7). Only an allowed, bound sender on ticket TIN-7125 reaches framing; any other message is dropped with a receipt row and no reply.

body_label.const: [Cade via swb: teammate information, not operator authority]

halt_ack_split.description: A halt ack has a null receipt and nothing to trim. When it is over 16384 bytes the receiver splits halted_jobs, in the order it stopped the jobs, across as many whole halted acks as it needs (wire contract section 5.4, round 4, R4-b).

reasons.description: Reply and refusal reasons. raised_by cade never reaches the wire: cade returns those from cade.dispatch.submit.

carve_out_match.description: A tag hits a carve-out tag when its normalized form contains a normalized carve-out stem (TIN-7125 contract-v1 section 6.1, round 3).

carve_out_goal_match.description: A goal hits a carve-out tag when its normalized form contains a normalized carve-out stem.

carve_out_normalize.description: Applied before matching: NFKC, then A-Z lowercased to a-z, then every character outside a-z and 0-9 removed.

carve_out_stems.description: The eight carve-out stems and the canonical tag each stands for. Every canonical tag contains its own stem, so a stamped canonical tag hits again.

carve_out_non_ascii.description: A raw tag with a non-ASCII letter after NFKC is refused with tag. A goal with one makes the carve-out status uncertain, which reroutes a Fable lane to Opus with goal as the reroute.

carve_out_accepted_gap.description: Inputs the carve-out rule knowingly leaves on a Fable root (wire contract section 6.1, round 4, R4-a). Jess ruled Current rule, accept the gap on TIN-7125 f38799d2. No resolver adds matching for these classes, and inside a job the carve-out holds for them only through section 6.2.

custody_labels.description: Custody from the source item's label (wire contract section 3.3).

trim.description: The characters normalize trims from both ends of a label: U+0009 to U+000D and U+0020, nothing else (wire contract section 3.3, round 4, R4-c).

custody_order.description: Custody classes from widest to narrowest. A child's custody may stay or move right, never left.

fable_model_id.description: The Fable id is a config value read from the account after login. The policy never carries a value.

on_unread.description: An unread Fable id refuses the job. It never waits on Opus and never runs on Opus.

config_dir.description: A Claude Code config dir of its own. Jess's own ~/.claude is never a job's.

login_isolation.description: Wire contract section 8. cade-job refuses with login-isolation unless the config dir and its login files are the job's own.

custody.description: Custody classes the lane admits from the source item's label. Each one must list the claude-code@cade harness seat, so confidential and health are out.

seats.description: Worker seats in preference order. Fable never runs a unit and Kimi never runs inside a Claude Code job.

seatId.description: First-class seat names. Adding a seat is a policy change, not a string edit.

providerId.description: Allow-listed providers. Adding one is a policy change, not a string edit.

custodyId.description: Cade custody classes. A child's custody class follows its parent home.

modelId.description: An exact model ID: a Claude ID such as claude-opus-5-5, the Kimi Code id k3.1-pro, or the forbidden Platform id kimi-k3.1-pro, which only a refused endpoint may list.

endpointId.description: Provider endpoints. Adding one is a policy change, not a string edit.

harnessSeatId.description: First-class harness-seat names. Adding one is a policy change, not a string edit.

harnessId.description: The agent harness a seat dispatches through. Kimi has no dispatch envelope of its own, so the Kimi reviewer rides the pi harness as pi-k3. Cade's job seat runs Claude Code.

dispatchRoute.description: Cade dispatch lanes (TIN-7125). Adding one is a policy change, not a string edit.

modelClass.description: A seat name, or the operator taking the lane personally.
